Hello, one and all.

As a new prepper, I think one of the most difficult things for me is staying motivated and on-task with my weekly goals of preparation. Thus, I had the idea to start this thread for those like myself who would like to find one or several others to stay accountable in making progress. This is not primarily for finding other preppers around your area, though I'm certain you could make the effort if you wanted. Perhaps some of the more experienced preppers around here would be willing to take a newbie or two under their wings and guide them?

Some suggestions on information if you decide to make a post looking for others:

  • How many people you want to team up with

  • How long you've been prepping

  • What you're hoping to accomplish

  • What you're knowledgeable / skilled at

  • What you want to learn or improve

  • Etc...

Hopefully this is helpful in getting some more momentum in new and experienced preppers alike. Community, knowledge, and motivation all work together for everyone's benefit.

I'm looking for two or three other people to team up with. I started taking prepping more seriously about three weeks ago, though I've dabbled in the idea on and off for a couple of months. Seeing as how I really see myself underprepared for any type of long-term hardship or disaster (or even just a survival situation), it'd be very helpful to find a couple other folks who want to stay motivated and on track with weekly goals of some sort.

I am most interested in food and water security, followed by acquiring and saving as much useful knowledge as possible. I am interested in learning and perfecting some survival skills, of course, but I think having a trove of useful knowledge available can be very valuable to use for any number of situations that come up later.

Feel free to reply to this post or PM me, whichever is better for you.

At least for me, it wasn't weekly goals that got me to what I have today (which isn't a huge amount but I'm satisfied at this point). I tackled it one project at a time. If weekly goals make more sense for you then do that. What I did was take one aspect of prepping and work on that for a while until I was comfortable with it. Then I move for a while to something else and eventually circle back to my first thing and work to improve that again.

Over the past couple years I've gone from some flashlights, a buck knife, a FM radio some energy bars and a water bottle in an old school bag to having a number of knives and fire arms, 20gal of clean water stored and a rain catching system to replenish, quite a bit of food stored and am currently working on a garden. I also have backup batteries for most of my electronics and working on a way to generate and store electricity. I have also stepped up my comms game quite a bit by getting into amateur radio. All on a shoestring budget with a family to support.

At this point I feel like I'd be far better off than the average person if things got bad... maybe not the average prepper but it's not like I'm finished or anything. One thing I need to work on is my fitness level. I'm out of shape and I need to start concentrating on that.
